title: A status change is refused once the user can no longer delete parts
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a custom role for this test, role D, with Part Library & Inventory — View, Part Library & Inventory — Create & Edit, Part Library & Inventory — Delete and See Financial Data, so user D starts with the right to delete parts.
  • Create a staff member for this test, user D, at the test location with role D.
  • Use two browser windows: window 1 signed in as the Admin, window 2 (a private window) signed in as user D.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B, that sit on no work order and no return.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Start window 1 on role D's Edit Role page (Roles & Permissions), with nothing changed yet.
  • Start window 2 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with the shared start of the part numbers typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. In window 2, click the three-dot actions button (⋮).
  2. In window 2, click Deactivate parts.
  3. In window 2, click the part A row.
  4. In window 2, click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  5. In window 1, untick Part Library & Inventory — Create & Edit.
  6. In window 1, untick Part Library & Inventory — Delete.
  7. In window 1, untick See Financial Data.
  8. In window 1, untick every permission in the Settings group.
  9. In window 1, click Save.
  10. In window 2, click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  11. In window 2, click the X at the right end of the dark bar.
  12. In window 2, click the part B row.
  13. In window 2, click Delete Part.
  14. In window 1, click Parts in the top bar.
  15. In window 1, click Inventory in the left menu.
  16. In window 1, type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens for user D.

Step 2:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 3:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation opens. Leave it open.

Step 5:

  • The Create & Edit box is unticked.

Step 6:

  • The Delete box is unticked.

Step 7:

  • The See Financial Data box is unticked.

Step 8:

  • Every Settings permission is unticked.

Step 9:

  • Role D is saved with only Part Library & Inventory — View left in the Part Library and Inventory group: user D now cannot delete inventory parts.

Step 10:

  • An access error appears saying user D is not allowed to do this (access denied).
  • No "1 part updated." message appears.

Step 11:

  • Bulk mode ends in window 2.

Step 12:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part B, still showing Delete Part (the page was loaded before the role changed).

Step 13:

  • An access error appears saying user D is not allowed to do this in the same way as for the status change, and the window stays open: the status change and the delete were refused alike for the same user.

Step 14:

  • Window 1 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 15:

  • Window 1 shows the Inventory page on the Active tab.

Step 16:

  • Part A and part B are both still listed on the Active tab: part A's status did not change and part B was not deleted.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10821 (Story 8, Permissions)

  • S8-N3: “If that user tries to set a part active or inactive by any route, the request is refused with an access denied error.”
  • S8-R15: “The system accepts a status change, a tracking change and an untracked part from exactly the users it accepts an inventory part delete from today.”
  • Story 8, context note: “Context note: S8-N1 to S8-N3 hold for a user who cannot delete inventory parts today. The system checks that access itself, so hiding the controls is not the only protection.”
  • Story 8, context note: “Context note (S8-R14, S8-R15): this spec does not change who can do what. Several role settings carry the right to delete inventory parts behind the scenes, and that stays exactly as it is today.”
